actual_defects_before_correction: Both public APIs accepted the first unsafe integer (2^53) and usize::MAX on the 64-bit host, while Source and fixture admission rejected those arguments.
Native excerpt collection eagerly built all text-block references before applying its redaction window.
implemented_behavior: Both public APIs return Result<String, PromptExcerptError>, with the exact Source safe-limit display text. Validation precedes document access or Value serialization.
The actual private production iterator reads only the first long text in the bounded lookup test. A separate late-tool_result control preserves the full candidate-turn type scan.
Both runtime callers use the known safe bound of 501. The combined 1,209-test workspace run verifies their integration.
explicit_api_migrations: Live host accessors are not representable as parsed JsDocument or serde_json::Value inputs. Actual host-object consumers are rejected by the compiler; the Source accessor operations remain distinct.
Negative, fractional, nonfinite and string arguments cannot be usize values. Source failures retain the genuine primitives; native compiler rejection is a separate migration.
The native String return changes to Result<String, PromptExcerptError>. Legal Result consumers compile; old unchecked String consumers fail.
The Value convenience facade serializes its complete input after validation. Lazy document lookup does not exclude that conversion work.
